chapter_seo_title: Fear - Li Huowang Investigates Pi County’s Rot | Dao-Twisted Chapter 271
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang uses invisibility to probe a terrified town and finds a sanitized gazetteer, hidden screams, and a family performing a ritual of agony with an iron clamp.
og_title: Chapter 271 — The Rain That Betrays You
og_description: Li Huowang’s camouflage has one flaw: the rain traces his shape. What he finds in a corrupt county yamen is worse than any monster.
twitter_title: Pi County’s secret is in the gazetteer—and in the woodshed.
twitter_description: Two years of silence. A child being pulled apart by his own parents. Li Huowang can turn invisible, but he can’t unsee this.

lore_anchors.definition: A local administrative record of major events, maintained by the county magistrate. In imperial China, these were official documents—a sanitized or empty gazetteer is evidence of deliberate cover-up.
A Chinese folk term for a solar eclipse. The celestial dog biting the sun was considered an omen of chaos; in the Dao-Twisted World, it may have literal, catastrophic consequences.
A classical Chinese historical phrase describing the ultimate famine horror: families swapping children to eat because they cannot bear to consume their own. Recorded in ancient annals as fact.
